properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's active development is not its stable product. MMS 4 stores models in SQL; the successor, Flexo / MMS 5, moves to an RDF quadstore and is described as 'GitHub for graphs', exposing SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and a SysML v2 API. A separate experimental SysML v2 execution environment (`Systemica`, Go) is also under way. Commits across those repositories were days old when reviewed (July–August 2026), so this is a live bet, not an aspiration. WHERE reflow2 STANDS: it has its own vocabulary — 29 node types, 60 edge types — and no standard interchange of any kind. It publishes three interfaces (`ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export`, `ifc:mcp-tools`), and `export_surface` already emits a subset of a design deliberately. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER TO ADOPT SysML v2 INTERNALLY — the vocabulary is load-bearing and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` and `req:functional-vocabulary-computes` both depend on it — but whether reflow2 should be able to SPEAK it at the edge, in and out. THE ARGUMENT FOR: Anthony works in a defence/aerospace systems-engineering context and will be asked, professionally, why a design tool does not interoperate with the standard his field is converging on. An export that a SysML v2 service can ingest is a different claim from an export only reflow2 reads. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: SysML v2 is large, its tooling is young, and a partial mapping that silently drops what it cannot express would be worse than none — reflow2's whole posture is that a lossy translation must be reported, not quietly performed. Mapping 29 types onto SysML v2 would need the same no-silent-drop discipline `changelog_view` holds with `unmapped`. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether a faithful SUBSET mapping exists that reports what it could not carry.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 speak SysML v2 at its boundary, given that is where the standards gravity has moved?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request to capture, as proposed ideas, the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger than reflow2 — before a deep review he intends to run against a clone of their repository. The strength claimed here is narrow and should be read narrowly: OpenMBEE has committed to a standard interchange and reflow2 has none. Whether their SysML v2 implementation is any good is exactly what the deep review is for, and nothing in this node asserts that it is.
